Portland Cement Association (2002). 2000 U.S. and Canadian Labor-Energy Input Survey. Economic Research Department (W.D. Toal, D.E. Czechowski), PCA, released March 2002. 46 pages. No report number or DOI printed.

Locators are the printed page numbers in the page footers (PDF page = printed + 2). Annual survey of PCA member plants (95 US, all 15 Canadian grey cement plants); white cement and grinding-only plants excluded. All energy is per EQUIVALENT tonne = 92% clinker + 8% finished cement (energy weights), for the whole plant including grinding. US figures are HHV in million Btu per metric tonne; Canadian figures LHV in GJ per tonne, so the two cannot be compared directly (3-7% difference). Loaded: the nine kiln-process categories of the "Summary report" pages (US wet, no preheater, preheater, precalciner, preheater-or-precalciner; Canada no preheater, preheater, precalciner, preheater/precalciner): fuel total, electricity, coal, petroleum coke, natural gas, oil products and waste fuels. Electricity kWh/t is derived from the printed kWh and the equivalent tonnage. Canadian wet-process data are withheld for 2000 (disclosure) - the 1996 value (6.141 GJ/t) is in the other-values series. Size, vintage and aggregate groupings are in other-values. Labour productivity data (employee-hours) not loaded: out of scope. Traps: "Dry process - Preheater or Precalciner" category includes preheater-only plants (US footnote); US "Preheater/Precalciner" 1972 value includes preheater only. No money values.
